topology.note: docker compose ps after bringing up dashboard + 3 gateway replicas + nginx

sse_through_nginx_proof.note: real event: snapshot frames with real RisingWave data and honest stale=true flags arrived every ~3s, unbuffered by nginx (proxy_buffering off took effect -- frames did not batch)

failover_demonstration.honest_claim: the long-lived SSE TCP connection to gateway-2 necessarily dropped when that container was killed -- this is expected, not a bug, and is NOT claimed as a dropped-connection-free failover

reconnect.note: the reconnect (simulating EventSource's own browser-native auto-reconnect) landed on gateway-3, not gateway-1 or the dead gateway-2 -- nginx's passive upstream health check correctly routed around the killed replica, and the new connection resumed real snapshots immediately, not a cached/fabricated one

health_endpoint.method: GET http://localhost:8088/health immediately after the kill

real_rag_query.method: POST http://localhost:8088/v1/rag/query (real embedding, real pgvector retrieval, real Ollama llama3.1:8b generation, real output rails) after gateway-2 was restarted
real_rag_query.result: 200 OK, answer="Apple's 2024 total net sales were $391.035 billion.", confidence=high, 1 citation to a real retrieved 10-K chunk
real_rag_query.note: GEMINI_MODE and KAFKA_MODE are disabled for this demo topology -- zero Gemini calls, and this demo traffic is not written into the real rag_events/judge_verdicts pipeline Day 6/7's calibration data lives in

failover_demonstration.no_fabricated_state_during_the_gap: the gap between the dropped connection and the resumed one shows no snapshot at all client-side (an honest disconnect), never a frozen or synthetic value standing in for the missing live connection

topology_after_restoring_gateway-2.note: gateway-2 was restarted via `docker compose up -d gateway-2` after the failover proof, to leave the full 3-replica topology intact

deliberate_spof: the dashboard/metrics service is a single container, not replicated, in this phase -- it is Option C's one internal dependency. A dashboard failure would stop new snapshots from reaching any gateway replica's poller, which would then emit unavailable snapshots (see finsentry/gateway/metrics_poller.py's unavailable_snapshot) rather than fabricate data; the dashboard itself is not fronted by nginx and not demonstrated as highly available in Day 8.
